headline: Tether Insiders Seek to Turn Gold Into a 4% Yield Machine
author: Ryan Weeks and Jack Ryan

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- Two executives with close ties to stablecoin giant Tether are raising money for a fund which will offer yield on digital assets backed by gold, at a time when the cryptocurrency issuer extends its reach in the bullion market.

Kintsugi Capital has been set up to offer yield on XAUt, Tether's gold-backed token, through strategies including hedged staking and lending, as well as basis and options trades, according to investment materials reviewed by Bloomberg News. Hedged staking involves earning rewards by locking up cryptocurrencies to help operate a blockchain network while using derivatives to reduce the risk of price swings.

Kintsugi, which has a direct partnership with Tether, will target a net yield of around 4% above returns from simply holding gold, according to the materials. It aims to grow to more than $100 million in assets under management within its first 12 months of operations, the materials show.

Alessandro Giori, who from 2024 served as global senior strategic partnership manager and head of Middle East and North Africa for Tether, leads the fund as chief executive officer, alongside Tether adviser Koh Onozawa Martinez, the materials show.
Kintsugi and Tether didn't respond to requests for comment.

Tether, issuer of the world's largest stablecoin USDT, has aggressively expanded into commodities markets in recent years, amassing gold reserves worth more than $19 billion by the end of September, one of the world's largest private stockpiles of the precious metal. It has simultaneously emerged as a bullion lender, providing about $1.5 billion in financing to a top US gold dealer.

Stablecoins such as USDT are designed to maintain a price closely correlated to a traditional asset like the US dollar, typically achieved by managing a reserve of cash-like assets. In a recent assessment of USDT's backing, S&P Global Ratings noted that the stablecoin's exposure to risky assets has increased over the past year. After a rally in gold prices, bullion holdings in the reserve accounted for about 10% of USDT in circulation, compared with 7% in September 2025.

Tether cut some of those gold holdings for the first time since 2024 in the most recent quarter, reducing them by 3.4 tons after a period of rapid accumulation, according to figures in its latest attestation report.
Tether also issues XAUt, a digital asset backed by physical gold. It is the largest of its kind, with a market capitalization of roughly $3 billion.

Kintsugi was named after the Japanese art of fixing broken pottery with gold, the materials show. Its fund will be regulated in the Cayman Islands, and overseen by a British Virgin Islands division of Further Asset Management, an Abu Dhabi-headquartered asset management group.
